findings.title: OptimizedCursorPaginator uses numeric key logic for a datetime-ordered endpoint
findings.body: OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key() does math.floor/math.ceil directly on getattr(item, self.key) and value_from_cursor() returns cursor.value unchanged. The only caller orders by '-datetime', so the key value is a datetime: math.floor(datetime) raises TypeError when build_cursor computes cursors, and build_queryset receives a raw numeric timestamp instead of the datetime that DateTimePaginator.value_from_cursor() reconstructs via datetime.fromtimestamp(.../multiplier). The optimized audit-log path therefore crashes or filters incorrectly on any non-empty page and is not cursor-compatible with DateTimePaginator.

findings.title: Negative queryset slicing raises AssertionError, contrary to claimed ORM handling
findings.body: When enable_advanced_features is set and a user-supplied cursor has offset < 0, this passes queryset[start_offset:stop] with a negative start (and possibly negative stop) to Django. Django QuerySets explicitly raise 'AssertionError: Negative indexing is not supported' for such slices; it does not handle boundary conditions automatically as the comment claims. A crafted cursor such as '0:-1:0' from a superuser/global-access user therefore produces an unhandled 500 instead of a 400/BadPaginationError, unlike OffsetPaginator/CombinedQuerysetPaginator which validate offset < 0.

findings.title: BasePaginator change affects all paginators and still allows negative prev offsets to crash
findings.body: BasePaginator.get_result is shared by Paginator, DateTimePaginator and subclasses across the API, not just audit logs. The change silently clamps negative offsets to 0 for non-prev cursors (masking malformed/tampered cursors and returning the first page) while leaving offset untouched for is_prev cursors, so queryset[offset:stop] with a negative prev offset still raises Django's negative-indexing AssertionError and returns 500. This is a global contract/behaviour change introduced under an audit-log optimization with no validation at Cursor.from_string either.

findings.title: Undocumented optimized_pagination switches cursor format for privileged users
findings.body: The new 'optimized_pagination=true' query parameter is not declared in AuditLogQueryParamSerializer or the published API schema, and it switches the endpoint from DateTimePaginator cursors (millisecond timestamp values) to OptimizedCursorPaginator cursors (raw integer key values). A client that obtains a cursor from one mode and replays it in the other, or toggles the flag, gets incorrect filtering/results. The gate also expands to any member with has_global_access, not just superusers as the 'authorized administrators' comment implies, exposing the untested code path broadly within an organization.

findings.title: No tests for OptimizedCursorPaginator or the optimized audit-log path
findings.body: The PR adds a new paginator class, a new negative-offset branch, a change to shared BasePaginator slicing, and a new endpoint branch, but adds no tests. Existing paginator/audit-log tests exercise DateTimePaginator only, so the datetime key mismatch, negative-offset AssertionError, and cursor incompatibility above are not caught. Tests should cover positive/prev/negative cursors, empty and non-empty datetime-ordered pages, and the endpoint with and without optimized_pagination for eligible and ineligible users before merging.
